address: 18th Cross Rd, Sector 2, HSR Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560102
review_text: ⚠️ Caution About Food Coloring – Cafe 27, HSR Layout  I ordered Barbeque Alfaham from Cafe 27, HSR Layout. After eating, I noticed a dark red color stuck to my fingers that did not wash off even after using handwash multiple times.  I spoke to the staff at the counter, and after checking with the chef, they said food coloring was added. They also mentioned that colors are added to kebabs and other chicken/fish fried items.  Adding artificial color to food without informing customers is concerning, especially from a health and safety perspective.  I’m sharing this so others can eat carefully and be cautious when ordering items that may contain added colors from this place.

address: 18th Cross Rd, Sector 2, HSR Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560102
review_text: One of my absolute go to places for Kerala food in Bangalore. There’s no doubt about this place  . It delivers the kind of comfort food you'd get back home in Kerala, especially if you're from the Malabar region.  We had nei pathiri, puttu, and poori and every dish was spot on in taste and texture. Just the thought of their nei pathiri with chicken curry is enough to make you drool!  Lunch here is equally satisfying the sambar is perfectly balanced, which is rare to find, and the fish fry is consistently delicious.  If you're craving simple, soulful Malabar food, Cafe 27 is the place. Highly recommended for a homely Kerala meal.

Whether you're a Keralite far from home or just a food enthusiast looking for a taste adventure, Cafe 27 is a must-visit. I can say, you won't be disappointed! 😍  So, what are you waiting for? Your taste buds will thank you!  *Rating:* 5/5 stars ⭐️ (and I'm not biased at all... okay, maybe a little 😉)  *Will I return?* Oh, you bet I will! 🎉 See you at Cafe 27, tea lovers! 😂

address: 18th Cross Rd, Sector 2, HSR Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560102
review_text: I had a disappointing experience at this cafe, mainly due to the behavior of the tea maker. The process is confusing for first-time visitors — you have to pay first, get a token, and then hand it to the tea maker. However, instead of simply accepting the token or explaining what to do, the tea maker insists that customers place the token in a very specific spot without clearly communicating where that is.  New customers are left puzzled, especially when there’s a long queue. Rather than guiding them politely, the tea maker responds rudely, which makes the whole experience uncomfortable. It would really help if the management put up clear instructions or had someone else handle the tea orders.  To be honest, the tea wasn’t anything special, and with this kind of customer service, it makes you question whether it’s worth coming back. I hope they improve the service soon, as this kind of attitude can drive regulars away.

review_text: A Taste of Kerala: Cafe 27 Review Cafe 27 offers a satisfying taste of Kerala. Their authentic Kerala meals are a standout, with flavors that transport you straight to the southern state. The unlimited rice is a generous touch, ensuring you leave feeling fully satisfied. While the fish fry, including matthi (sardine) and aila (bangda), was decent, it could have been a bit more flavorful. The chicken biryani, though authentic, might not quite match up to the best Kerala biryani you've had. However, the meals are definitely worth the price, especially considering the quality and quantity. The cafe can get quite crowded during peak lunch hours, so be prepared for a wait. If you're looking for a quick bite, their tea and other Kerala snacks are also worth trying. Ample parking space is a definite plus. Overall, Cafe 27 is a reliable choice for authentic Kerala cuisine.

review_text: After recently visiting Alappuzha for Onam, I was craving Kerala's banana fritters and tea. I decided to visit this place, as I have known this shop since it operated from a small hut across the road from its current location. Over the years, I have noticed a clear pattern in how they treat customers.  Despite being a long-time visitor, the staff and management consistently seem to prioritize Malayali customers, making others feel less welcome. THEY GIVE PREFERENCE ONLY TO MALYALIS . This behavior has been DISAPPOINTING, and while I have overlooked it in the past because the food is occasionally good, today I was especially frustrated. The preference given to Malayalis was so blatant that, out of anger, I threw my chai glass into the pot instead of putting it back at the tea stall .  I regret letting my frustration get the better of me, but it reflects how upsetting the experience was. Food is one thing, but customer service and respect should be consistent, regardless of where someone is from
